lines.text: At the start of the year, our form teacher brought a hamster to class.
She said that looking after a animal would teach us to be responsible.
lines.note: Article: 'animal' starts with a vowel sound, so it is 'an animal'.

lines.text: We named the hamster Pepper, and we take turns to feed it every morning.
Pepper sleep for most of the day in a small house made of
lines.note: Agreement: 'Pepper' is one animal, so it is 'sleeps'.

lines.text: cardboard. In the afternoon, it wakes up and runs on its wheel for hour.
lines.note: Plural: it runs for a long time, so it is 'for hours'.

lines.text: Last month, Pepper escape from its cage during a science lesson.
lines.note: Tense: 'last month' is in the past, so it is 'escaped'.

lines.text: The whole class searched the room careful, looking under every desk and bag.
lines.note: Word form: 'searched' is a verb, so it takes the adverb 'carefully'.

lines.text: After twenty minute, somebody heard a scratching sound inside the teacher’s cupboard.
Pepper had climbed into a box of old worksheets and fallen asleep there.
Since that day, two of we check the cage door before every lesson.
Our teacher were right: we have all become more careful and more patient.
lines.note: Agreement: 'our teacher' is one person, so it is 'was'.

lines.text: Pepper, of course, has learnt nothing at all.
